On May 9, 2025, a confrontation and subsequent skirmish between law enforcement and four [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] politicians occurred at [[Delaney Hall]], an immigration detention center in [[Newark, New Jersey]], United States. 

[[Ras Baraka]], the [[List of mayors of Newark, New Jersey|mayor of Newark]], was arrested and charged with trespassing, but the charges were later dropped. [[LaMonica McIver]], one of the three [[New Jersey's congressional delegations|U.S. representatives from New Jersey]] involved, was later charged with three counts of assaulting or interfering with a federal officer. McIver rejected the charges as an attempt at political intimidation.

==Background==

=== Congressional authority ===
Members of [[United States Congress|Congress]] have legal authority to conduct unannounced oversight visits at detention centers run by the [[United States Department of Homeland Security|Department of Homeland Security]] (DHS).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Santana |first=Rebecca |date=2025-05-14 |title=ICE head recognizes Congress' role in visiting detention facilities, even unannounced |url=https://apnews.com/article/immigration-customs-enforcement-detention-trump-deportations-a6db9cf486c9556534ac08a15ced9959 |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Facility Visits for Members of Congress and Staff |url=https://www.ice.gov/doclib/detention/iceFacilityVisitationCongressional.pdf |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623201803/https://www.ice.gov/doclib/detention/iceFacilityVisitationCongressional.pdf |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

=== Delaney Hall ===
{{main|Delaney Hall}}
Delaney Hall is a 1,000-bed immigrant detention center in [[Newark, New Jersey]], operated by [[GEO Group]], an institutional facilities company. The facility opened in 2000 and closed in 2017. [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) awarded GEO Group a {{USD|1}} billion contract for fifteen years to reopen Delaney Hall in February 2025. The contract included funds to establish a federal immigration processing center. The detention center began receiving migrants in May. It is the largest detention center on the [[East Coast of the United States]].<ref name=":Raji">{{Cite news |last1=Raji |first1=Tobi |last2=Hernández |first2=Arelis |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2025/05/10/delaney-hall-detention-facility-explained/ |title=What to know about Delaney Hall, where Newark's mayor was arrested |date=May 10, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref>

Several protests have occurred at Delaney Hall, including daily prayer vigils. Newark sued GEO Group in New Jersey Superior Court in March, alleging that the facility did not have a valid [[certificate of occupancy]]. In April, the case was transferred to federal court, where a judge was weighing Newark's request to close the facility "pending inspection and compliance with local, State, and administrative codes". The city's mayor, [[Ras Baraka]], told immigrant rights activists in March that he would padlock the building to prevent it from opening.<ref name=":Raji"/>

==Incident==
{{Further|List of immigrant detention sites in the United States}}
Sometime between 1:00{{nbsp}}pm<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Kudacki |first=Andres |date=2025-05-12 |title=How it unfolded: The arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka at the controversial Delaney Hall New Jersey ICE site |url=https://jerseyvindicator.org/2025/05/12/how-it-unfolded-the-arrest-of-newark-mayor-ras-baraka-at-the-controversial-delaney-hall-new-jersey-ice-site/ |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=The Jersey Vindicator |language=en-US}}</ref> and 1:15{{nbsp}}pm<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last1=Davis |first1=Aaron C. |last2=Baran |first2=Jonathan |date=2025-05-22 |title=Body slamming? Officer aggression? How an ICE clash led to charges against a congresswoman. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/investigations/2025/05/22/lamonica-mciver-congresswoman-charges-ice/ |access-date=2025-05-24 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> on May 9, 2025, three [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[United States House of Representatives|representatives]] from [[New Jersey]]—[[Bonnie Watson Coleman]], [[Rob Menendez]], and [[LaMonica McIver]]—arrived at Delaney Hall for an unscheduled oversight visit. They went up to the gated fence separating the parking area on the grounds of Delaney Hall from the public property outside the premises, and they spoke to the guards through the fence, explaining who they are and that members of Congress can make unannounced oversight visits to detention facilities. After a few minutes, the gate opened to allow a car to enter, and the three representatives walked onto the grounds before the gate closed. They spoke further with the guards, and soon after, DHS officers approached and took them to a waiting room inside Delaney Hall.<ref name=":1" /> Menendez later said that they were then "told to wait for ICE brass from Newark to arrive."<ref name=":8">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CUjfHM8l1QQ |title='Never seen anything like it in my life': New Jersey congressman reacts to Newark mayor arrest |date=2025-05-09 |last=MSNBC |access-date=2025-05-25 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

Baraka arrived around 1:40{{nbsp}}pm, and he initially remained on the public property outside the premises. A number of protesters were also on the public property. About ten minutes later, as Baraka was speaking to a guard on the other side of the fence, the guard opened the gate and allowed Baraka and his bodyguards to enter the grounds, where they then waited near the gate, which closed after they were let in.<ref name=":0" /> The video footage contradicts accusations that he had barged into the facility without permission.<ref name=":Ferre">{{Cite web |last=Ferré-Sadurní |first=Luis |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/19/nyregion/new-jersey-congress-ice-charges.html |title=Rep. McIver Charged With Assault Over Clash Outside Newark ICE Center |date=May 19, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> Baraka later stated that the guard had invited him in, saying that it might "calm the crowd" of protesters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fernandez |first=Madison |last2=Rivard |first2=Ry |last3=Cheney |first3=Kyle |last4=Gerstein |first4=Josh |date=2025-06-03 |title=New Jersey mayor sues Trump ally Alina Habba over charge |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/03/nj-mayor-sues-alina-habba-00382249 |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref>

At 2:33{{nbsp}}pm, several [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Homeland Security Investigations]] (HSI) officers came out of Delaney Hall, walked over to where Baraka was waiting, and asked him to leave the property, telling him that he would be arrested otherwise.<ref name=":0" /> Watson Coleman later said that she, McIver, and Menendez had been in the waiting room up until that point, waiting for their oversight tour, and that "all of the ICE officials from the state of New Jersey at the highest levels came to the detention facility, and we thought it was to resolve our issue of taking the tour. So they came, they said hello, and the next thing we saw, they ran outside." The three members of Congress followed them out and saw that the mayor was there. The officers were talking to him, and the lawmakers walked over to join the discussion.<ref name=":2">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=90JigIJpFwA |title='This is un-American': Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman on the arrest of Newark mayor at ICE facility |date=2025-05-09 |last=MSNBC |access-date=2025-05-24 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

The officials told Baraka that he would be arrested if he didn't leave. One of the HSI officers displayed handcuffs, which McIver called "unnecessary" and "ugly". Watson Coleman encouraged everyone to remain calm, and she and Baraka walked together to the gate after one of the officers said "All right, then. Walk out." At 2:39{{nbsp}}pm, the gate opened, and Baraka and his bodyguards walked through and back onto the public property outside the premises.<ref name=":1" /> The gate closed, and through the fence, Watson Coleman told Baraka "We will be your eyes and your ears and we will report to you, mayor."<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last1=Gerstein |first1=Josh |last2=Rivard |first2=Ry |date=2025-05-20 |title=New Jersey Rep. LaMonica McIver faces felony assault charges in conflict at ICE facility, court filing shows |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/20/lamonica-iver-assault-charge-00358400 |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref>

The three members of Congress then walked back across the grounds towards the Delaney Hall entrance. Watson Coleman later said that they thought they would finally be able to have their oversight tour, but "noticed that ICE and officials were huddling and having a discussion", so they decided to "wait and see what was going on." She, McIver, and Menendez saw that the officials were on the phone with someone and then heard one of them say that they were going to arrest Baraka,<ref name=":2" /> at which point Menendez walked back to the gate to alert him, again talking with him through the fence.<ref name=":1" /> Baraka responded that they couldn't arrest him because he was no longer on ICE property.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last1=Paúl |first1=María Luisa |last2=Kaur |first2=Anumita |last3=Tucker |first3=Brianna |date=2025-05-09 |title=Newark mayor charged with trespassing after arrest at ICE detention center |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2025/05/09/newark-mayor-ice-arrest-ras-baraka-nj/ |access-date=2025-05-24 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

Somewhere between 12<ref name=":1" /> and 20<ref name=":0" /> ICE and HSI officers then grouped on the Delaney Hall side of the gate, and at 2:44{{nbsp}}pm, it opened, and they moved onto the public property to arrest Baraka.<ref name=":0" /> The three members of Congress followed them out the gate.<ref name=":1" /> An aide to Watson Coleman started yelling "Circle the mayor, circle the mayor",<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Strunsky |first=Steve |date=2025-05-14 |title=Watch: N.J. mayor charged with trespassing at ICE center was let in by guard, new video shows |url=https://www.nj.com/essex/2025/05/newark-mayor-releases-video-to-refute-trespassing-charges-at-ice-detention-center.html |access-date=2025-05-24 |website=NJ.com |language=en}}</ref> and several people—including the members of Congress, aides, and protesters—encircled Baraka, forming a human shield in an attempt to prevent the arrest. The ICE and HSI officers tried to push through to Baraka, and McIver was heard saying "Don't touch us, don't touch us."<ref name=":1" /> McIver, Watson Coleman, and Baraka were next to each other at the center of the crowd.<ref name=":4" /> It turned into a melee with people pushing and shoving. Some in the crowd were yelling to the officers "Don't touch her" and "Don’t put your hands on her", apparently referring to the two congresswomen.<ref name=":3" />

The chaotic scrum continued for about 90 seconds, with the officers attempting to pry Baraka from the group in order to arrest him. Eventually the officers pulled Baraka away from the people trying to shield him. According to ''[[The Washington Post]]'', "Video captures multiple instances in the scrum when McIver and federal agents made physical contact, beginning with one in which a Homeland Security agent gripped her arm and she pulled her hand up to break away."<ref name=":1" /> ''The Jersey Vindicator'' reported that she also yelled "'Get your hands off of me' after an agent grabs her shoulders."<ref name=":0" /> The ''[[Associated Press]]'' stated that "At one point her left elbow and then her right elbow push into an officer wearing a dark face covering and an olive green uniform emblazoned with the word 'Police' on it. It isn't clear from bodycam video whether that contact was intentional, incidental or a result of jostling in the chaotic scene."<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Catalini |first=Mike |date=2025-05-21 |title=New Jersey Democratic Rep. McIver released on recognizance on federal assault charges |url=https://apnews.com/article/lamonica-mciver-ice-assault-charge-new-jersey-2e6403ecb933882e641557303cdc6b2a |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> During this time, one video showed an officer who "lifts a weapon with a long black barrel that he holds with both hands and points it at various people in the crowd" without firing.<ref name=":4" /> Menendez said later that all of the officers were armed.<ref name=":8" />

After pulling Baraka away, the federal officers arrested him, handcuffed him, and took him back onto the Delaney Hall grounds.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last1=Enuco |first1=Matthew |last2=Strunsky |first2=Steve |date=2025-05-12 |title=Did Democrats really 'storm' ICE facility and 'body slam' guards? Here's what the video shows. |url=https://www.nj.com/essex/2025/05/did-democrats-really-storm-ice-facility-and-body-slam-guards-heres-what-the-videos-show.html |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=NJ.com |language=en}}</ref> This occurred at about 2:46{{nbsp}}pm, and 20 minutes later, vehicles exited the grounds, taking Baraka to an ICE field office elsewhere in Newark.<ref name=":0" /> Meanwhile, the three members of Congress, still being jostled, worked their way back onto the Delaney Hall grounds, where McIver exchanged words with some of the officers.<ref name=":6" /> She was "heard screaming at officers and saying, 'Ma'am, he just assaulted me.'"<ref name=":Ferre" /> As McIver attempted to get back onto the grounds, ''[[The New York Times]]'' described her as both "pushing toward the gates and being pushed from behind".<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |last=Tully |first=Tracey |date=2025-05-26 |title=New to Congress, She's in the Cross Hairs of Trump's Justice Department |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/26/nyregion/lamonica-mciver-newark-assault-charges.html |access-date=2025-05-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>  Then the three lawmakers went back into Delaney Hall, where they were finally given their oversight tour.<ref name=":6" />

The lawmakers left Delaney Hall at 3:48{{nbsp}}pm, and held a short press conference on the public property outside.<ref name=":0" /> McIver said that if the officers could treat a mayor and members of Congress as they did, they would not treat anyone with respect or dignity. Watson Coleman called what happened "the weaponization of law enforcement", and it meant that "none of us are safe."<ref name=":8" /> When the press conference ended, Watson Coleman and Menendez drove to the ICE field office where Baraka was being held, and waited with a crowd for his release. He was released about five hours after he was arrested.<ref name=":0" />

==Aftermath==
Baraka was federally charged for allegedly trespassing.<ref name=":Tully-McFadden" >{{Cite web |last1=Tully |first1=Tracey |last2=McFadden |first2=Alyce |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/10/nyregion/newark-ice-protest-lawmakers-ras-baraka.html |title=3 Lawmakers Involved in Newark Protest Could Be Arrested, D.H.S. Says |date=May 10, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> He later briefly returned to Delaney Hall<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sheldon |first1=Chris |last2=Strunsky |first2=Steve |url=https://www.nj.com/essex/2025/05/newark-mayor-returns-to-ice-detention-center-4-days-after-his-arrest.html |title=Newark mayor returns to ICE detention center, 4 days after his arrest |date=May 14, 2025 |publisher=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> and appeared in court on May 15, in a perfunctory hearing scheduling further action.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rivard |first=Ry |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/15/ras-baraka-trespassing-ice-trial-00351878 |title=Newark Mayor Ras Baraka headed to trial on trespassing charge after arrest at ICE facility |date=May 15, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> The previous day, Baraka released video clips showing him being allowed to enter the grounds, leaving the grounds, and later being arrested outside.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=News: Mayor Ras J. Baraka statement on provided video of his entry and exit at Delaney Hall last Friday |url=https://www.newarknj.gov/news/mayor-ras-j-baraka-statement-on-provided-video-of-his-entry-and-exit-at-delaney-hall-last-friday |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=City of Newark New Jersey}}</ref> 

The day of the arrest, the DHS released a statement alleging that "a group of protestors, including two members of the U.S. House of Representatives, stormed the gate and broke into the detention facility."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-09 |title=Members of Congress Break into Delaney Hall Detention Center |url=https://www.dhs.gov/news/2025/05/09/members-congress-break-delaney-hall-detention-center |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Department of Homeland Security |language=en}}</ref> DHS spokeswoman [[Tricia McLaughlin (government official)|Tricia McLaughlin]] indicated that Watson Coleman, Menendez, and McIver might face assault charges,<ref name=":Tully-McFadden" /> and stated that DHS had video of the three "assaulting" the officers, "including body slamming a female ICE officer."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kochi |first=Sudiksha |title=Dems face criminal probe after ICE detention center scuffle |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/05/11/dhs-investigating-democrats-baraka-ice-scuffle/83569622007/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> DHS [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary]] [[Kristi Noem]] later accused the lawmakers of "committing felonies{{nbsp}}... and attacking people who stand up for the rule of law."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fields |first=Ashleigh |date=2025-05-14 |title=Noem: Democratic lawmakers committed 'felonies' at ICE facility, calls for censuring |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5299452-homeland-security-secretary-accuses-democrats-felony/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=The Hill}}</ref>

Menendez said the melee could have been avoided, and the incident "should have ended" when Baraka walked out the gate and back onto the public property. He repeatedly described what occurred as a "clear act of intimidation", at one point saying that that "is what this administration is entirely about",<ref name=":8" /> and that it was "intended to intimidate not just the mayor, but the three of us and everyone watching today." McIver said "We were met with contempt, disrespect, and aggression from ICE. From roughing up members of congress to arresting the mayor of our state's largest city, there is no version of today that does not show the blatant abuses of power of the Trump administration."<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Oppenheim |first1=Oren |last2=Barr |first2=Luke |last3=Khan |first3=Mariam |last4=Katersky |first4=Aaron |last5=Margolin |first5=Josh |title=Newark Mayor Ras Baraka arrested at ICE facility while joining Democrats to conduct 'oversight' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/newark-mayor-arrested-ice-facility-joining-democrats-conduct/story?id=121652689 |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref> McIver alleged that the lawmakers had been "assaulted by multiple ICE agents".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coronell Uribe |first=Raquel |last2=Reilly |first2=Ryan J. |date=2025-05-19 |title=DOJ charges N.J. congresswoman with assaulting law enforcement at ICE facility |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/lamonica-mciver-ras-baraka-alina-habba-ice-new-jersey-newark-rcna207842 |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> Menendez added "It's something that I never thought I would see, to see how physical they were with the mayor of the largest city of New Jersey and three members of Congress."<ref name=":3" />

On May 19, [[Alina Habba]], the acting [[United States Attorney for the District of New Jersey|US attorney for the district of New Jersey]], announced that McIver had been charged with [[Assaulting, resisting, or impeding certain United States Government officers or employees|assaulting, impeding and interfering with law enforcement]], and the charges against Baraka had been dropped.<ref name=":Ferre" /> Habba had not yet sought a grand jury indictment against McIver. Federal rules gave her 30 days to do so.<ref name=":7" /> The criminal complaint against McIver alleges that she used "each of her forearms to forcibly strike" one officer, and "slammed her forearm" into another, "forcibly" grabbing him<ref name=":7" /> as she "reached out and tried to restrain" him.<ref name=":1" /> Menendez responded that officers had assaulted McIver and put their hands on all three of the lawmakers, and "the administration should be apologizing to Rep. McIver, not arresting her on unprecedented, politicized charges".<ref name=":7" /> McIver responded that the charges against her "mischaracterize and distort my actions" and were filed for political reasons.<ref name=":1" /> She also said that she had been offered a plea deal, but rejected it, as she would not admit to something she had not done.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=NJ congresswoman rejects plea deal, denies wrongdoing at ICE detention center |url=https://abc7ny.com/post/nj-rep-lamonica-mciver-rejects-plea-deal-denies-wrongdoing-ice-detention-center-delaney-hall-newark/16482891/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=ABC7 New York |language=en}}</ref> It is rare for sitting members of Congress to be charged with crimes other than fraud or corruption.<ref name=":9" />

A hearing on Baraka's trespassing charges was held on May 21 before federal [[magistrate]] judge Andre Espinosa, who formally dismissed the charges and spent several minutes criticizing the actions of the US attorney's office, calling Baraka's arrest "hasty" and "a worrying misstep". After the hearing, Baraka was heard on a [[hot mic]] saying "Jesus, he tore these people a new asshole."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blackburn |first=Zach |date=2025-05-21 |title=Judge dismisses Baraka charges, reprimands prosecutors |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/judiciary/judge-dismisses-baraka-charges-reprimands-prosecutors/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=New Jersey Globe |language=en-US}}</ref>

Also on May 21, McIver had a hearing before federal magistrate judge Stacey Adams, who released McIver on her own recognizance.<ref name=":9" /> One of the lawyers she hired, [[Paul J. Fishman]], previously held the position now held by Habba. McIver has stated that it will be expensive for her to fight the charges,<ref name=":12" /> leading some Democrats to send fundraising emails on her behalf.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=2025-05-29 |title=Trump has created a new Democratic superstar: LaMonica McIver |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/05/29/lamonica-mciver-trump-justice-department-ice |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref>

On June 3, 2025 Baraka filed suit against Habba and Ricky Patel, the HSI officer who supervised the arrest, for [[false arrest]] and [[malicious prosecution]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tully |first=Tracey |date=2025-06-03 |title=Newark’s Mayor Sues a Top Trump Lawyer, Claiming Malicious Prosecution |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/03/nyregion/ras-baraka-alina-habba-lawsuit-ice.html |access-date=2025-06-03 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> It also alleges that Habba [[Defamation|defamed]] him in her public comments about the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Catalini |first=Mike |date=2025-06-03 |title=Newark mayor sues New Jersey's top federal prosecutor after arrest at immigration detention site |url=https://apnews.com/article/newark-mayor-ras-baraka-lawsuit-arrest-immigration-0d17f4adb136b9fefc02ea8b498124ed |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

On June 10, 2025, Habba announced that a federal grand jury had indicted McIver on three counts of assaulting, resisting, impeding, and interfering with federal officials. McIver responded that the case is "a brazen attempt at political intimidation". The ''[[Associated Press]]'' reported that based on law enforcement bodycam video that has been made public, it is difficult to determine whether the allegations stem from "contact [that] was intentional, incidental or a result of jostling in the chaotic scene."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-10 |title=US Rep. LaMonica McIver indicted on federal charges from skirmish at New Jersey immigration center |url=https://apnews.com/article/lamonica-mciver-assault-charge-alina-habba-immigration-7b6a5b0fc8079a9efd0606ab68e3f02d |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> At her arraignment hearing, McIver pleaded not guilty, and Judge [[Jamel K. Semper|Jamel Semper]] set a trial date of November 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Catalini |first=Mike |date=2025-06-25 |title=US Rep. LaMonica McIver pleads not guilty to assault charges stemming from immigration center visit |url=https://apnews.com/article/lamonica-mciver-newark-new-jersey-immigration-991f84363c403c0ff5c970ad2bee64bb |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

In mid-August, McIver's lawyers filed several motions. They argued for dismissal on the grounds that she's protected by the [[Constitution of the United States|US Constitution's]] [[Speech or Debate Clause|speech or debate clause]], and that she is being selectively prosecuted. In another motion, they asked Semper to order the government to produce certain evidence they alleged it had failed to turn over. They also asked Semper to order the government to stop making prejudicial comments about the case in public.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blackburn |first=Zach |last2=Fox |first2=Joey |date=2025-08-18 |title=McIver, moving to dismiss charges, asks why she’s treated differently from Jan. 6 rioters |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/fr/mciver-moving-to-dismiss-charges-asks-why-shes-treated-differently-from-pardoned-jan-6-rioters/ |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=New Jersey Globe |language=en-US}}</ref> In one of their filings, the lawyers described some of the bodycam recordings that had been turned over. They said the footage included audio of the HSI official who had been on the phone before Baraka's arrest, and that the official told other officers that [[Todd Blanche]], the [[United States Deputy Attorney General|deputy attorney general]], had ordered the arrest. ''[[Politico]]'' identified that official as Ricky Patel, one of the people against whom Baraka has filed suit.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rivard |first=Ry |last2=Friedman |first2=Matt |last3=Orden |first3=Erica |date=2025-08-19 |title=‘We are arresting the mayor right now, per the deputy attorney general’ |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/18/newark-mayor-arrest-bodycam-footage-todd-blanche-00513734 |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=Politico}}</ref>

== Oversight ==
In a May 9 interview, Watson Coleman reported that their oversight tour showed that the facility was clean, but the detainees did not have the access that they should to immigration attorneys.<ref name=":2" />

==Responses==
The incident became a "partisan flashpoint", according to ''[[Politico]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rivard |first1=Ry |last2=Han |first2=Daniel |last3=Gerstein |first3=Josh |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/09/ice-releases-new-jersey-mayor-00340241 |title=ICE releases New Jersey mayor arrested at protest with lawmakers |date=May 9, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> The incident was widely discussed in [[Conservatism in the United States|conservative]] media, which repeated the claim that Democrats had "stormed" the facility. ''The New York Times'' reported that "Republicans have seized on the episode to portray Democrats as more interested in protecting the immigrants with criminal records they said are being held inside the facility than U.S. citizens", and that the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] had sought to cast the incident as "a violent mob attack on federal officers".<ref name=":Ferre" /> Both Democrats and Republicans pointed to video footage from body cameras of the incident to accuse each other of instigating the scuffle. ''The New York Times'' stated that the federal government's narrative that the lawmakers had "stormed" the facility was contradicted by video footage and several witnesses at the scene.<ref name=":Ferre" />

=== New Jersey ===
Baraka's arrest was condemned by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]], including state governor [[Phil Murphy]], senators [[Andy Kim]] and [[Cory Booker]],<ref name=":5">{{Cite news |last1=Tully |first1=Tracey |last2=Ferré-Sadurní |first2=Luis |last3=McFadden |first3=Alyce |date=2025-05-09 |title=Newark's Mayor Arrested at Protest Outside ICE Detention Center |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/09/nyregion/newark-ice-protest-arrest-ras-baraka.html |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> representatives [[Frank Pallone]],<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last1=Catalini |first1=Mike |last2=Richer |first2=Durkin |last3=Tucker |first3=Eric |date=2025-05-20 |title=Prosecutors charge McIver with pushing and grabbing agents while trying to stop mayor's arrest |url=https://apnews.com/article/new-jersey-mciver-habba-baraka-ice-facility-f4c995ea685e9085f585be345649f57a |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> [[Mikie Sherrill]] and [[Josh Gottheimer]], [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]] mayor [[Steven Fulop]], and former [[New Jersey Senate]] president [[Stephen Sweeney]].<ref name=":Rivard1" >{{Cite web |last=Rivard |first=Ry |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/09/new-jersey-mayor-ras-baraka-ice-00339287 |title=New Jersey Mayor Ras Baraka arrested at ICE facility |date=May 9, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> Kim said that he was discussing the incident with ICE officials and DHS secretary [[Kristi Noem]].<ref name=":5" /> [[Bob Hugin]], the [[New Jersey Republican State Committee Chairmen|chair of the New Jersey Republican Party]], former radio host [[Bill Spadea]], and former assemblyman [[Jack Ciattarelli]] condemned Baraka.<ref name=":Rivard1" />

Two hundred thirty-one faith leaders in the state signed a letter of support for McIver, saying that the charges are "a politically motivated campaign designed to tarnish the reputation of a public servant who has tirelessly fought for justice and equity."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wildstein |first=David |date=2025-05-30 |title=231 N.J. faith leaders stand with LaMonica McIver, call charges politically motivated |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/231-n-j-faith-leaders-stand-with-lamonica-mciver-call-charges-politically-motivated/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=New Jersey Globe |language=en-US}}</ref>

===National===
House minority leader [[Hakeem Jeffries]] and Senate minority leader [[Chuck Schumer]] defended Baraka on social media. 

The [[United States House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight|House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight]] announced a hearing into the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuchs |first=Hailey |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2025/05/16/congress/house-judiciary-subcommittee-to-examine-new-jersey-ice-facility-incident-00353395 |title=House Judiciary to examine New Jersey ICE facility incident |date=May 16, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> Representative [[Buddy Carter]] introduced a measure that would strip Coleman, Menendez, and McIver of their committee assignments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wu |first=Nicholas |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2025/05/13/congress/new-jersey-democrats-committees-buddy-carter-00345479 |title=GOP proposal would boot 3 NJ Democrats from House committees |date=May 13, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> Representative [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] said that McIver should be expelled from the House,<ref name=":Ferre" /> and on May 21, Representative [[Nancy Mace]] filed a resolution to do so.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fields |first=Ashleigh |date=2025-05-21 |title=Mace files resolution to expel McIver over ICE assault charges |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5312503-nancy-mace-resolution-expulse-rep-lamonica/ |access-date=2025-05-26 |work=The Hill}}</ref> Representative William Timmons filed a resolution to censure McIver.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mueller |first=Julia |last2=Beitsch |first2=Rebecca |date=2025-05-14 |title=Temperatures rise over House Democrats’ scuffle with ICE agents |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5301063-democrats-dhs-noem-ice-new-jersey/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |work=The Hill}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rivard |first1=Ry |last2=Han |first2=Daniel |last3=Coltin |first3=Jeff |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/12/a-new-jersey-mayors-arrest-at-ice-facility-fires-up-democrats-from-new-york-to-chicago-00342209 |title=A New Jersey mayor's arrest at ICE facility fires up Democrats from New York to Chicago |date=May 12, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |access-date=May 19, 2025}}</ref> [[Yvette Clarke|Yvette Clark]], chair of the [[Congressional Black Caucus]], said that Trump had "weaponized" the Department of Justice and was using McIver as "to intimidate Congress into submission".<ref name=":11" /> A group of eleven Republican former members of Congress released a statement condemning the charges. One of them, [[Claudine Schneider]], called it "outrageous" and said "Every member of Congress, both past and present, should be speaking up. If not, we will very soon lose our ability to do so."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wire |first=Sarah D. |date=May 22, 2025 |title=Former congressional Republicans decry 'extreme' charges against Rep. LaMonica McIver |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/05/22/congressional-republicans-decry-lamonica-mciver-doj-charges/83790762007/ |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-22 |title=Former GOP Members of Congress Reject Charges Against Congresswoman McIver |url=https://www.democracydefendersfund.org/prs/05.22.25-pr |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=Democracy Defenders Fund |language=en}}</ref> Senators [[Cory Booker]], [[Raphael Warnock]], [[Angela Alsobrooks]], and [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]] condemned the charges against McIver, describing them as "efforts to intimidate her and silence those who seek to hold this administration accountable", and as taking resources away from actual public safety concerns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-23 |title=Black US Senators Slam Charges Against Rep. LaMonica McIver, Demand Trump Admin Drop Case |url=https://www.essence.com/news/black-u-s-senators-slam-charges-against-rep-lamonica-mciver/ |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=Essence |language=en-US}}</ref> She has also received support from Democrats in the House, including [[Maxwell Frost]], [[Pramila Jayapal]], [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], and [[Delia Ramirez]].<ref name=":13" />

When asked, [[Donald Trump|President Trump]] said that he had "no idea" who McIver was, but "That woman was out of control".<ref name=":10" /> In a congressional hearing, Noem testified that a "mob of protesters including three members of Congress stormed the gate and they trespassed into the detention facility."<ref name=":1" />
